subject: K Fold Cross Validation - its explicit calculation

messages.author: 1fe638ac9008754d
messages.subject: K Fold Cross Validation - its explicit calculation
parts:
Hi,

I am estimating predictive performance by K Fold Cross Validation for a hierarchical model. (I have tried PSIS-LOO, but there are too many khats above 1 for it to be reliable.)

In each iteration I leave out one of the individual data sets, and draw parameters for the hold out set, from each parameter's respective posteriors (these parameters are called aLambda, and aKappa below.):

    aKappa <- exponential_rng(a[Index]);
    aLambda <- exponential_rng(b[Index]);

'bIndex' is a mid-level index here that specifies the particular posterior distribution corresponding to this hold out sample.

In the 'generated quantities' part of the Stan program, I capture the log probability from my model, for each of my nk data points in the hold out sample (Yk is the hold out dependent variable):

    for (i in 1:nk){
        ...
        lLogLikelihood[i] <- neg_binomial_2_log(Yk[i],aLambda,aKappa);
    }

I therefore end up with a nSamples x nk matrix of log probabilities. Let's call this mLogProb.

I am following Aki's et al. (2015) paper, 'Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC', to estimate the elpd. In each of the K iterations, I get this matrix mLogProb. My hold out data sets are, in general, of different sizes in each iteration. My question is, how can I use this series (mLogProb_1,mLogProb_2,...,mLog_k) to estimate the elpd? I'm just not quite understanding how I follow the paper here.

Finally, I'm wanting to calculate a standard error on this elpd. This is given by eqn. (23) in the paper. How can I estimate the standard error in elpd here?

Best,

Ben

Finally, I'm wanting to calculate a standard error on this elpd. This is given by eqn. (23) in the paper. How can I estimate the standard error in elpd here?

You can combine your matrices to one nSamples x n matrix (e.g. LogProb). Compute log of the expected predictive densities log(mean(exp(LogProb))) or the numerically more accurate version log_sum_exp(LogProb)-log(n), and you get 1xn vector elpd values. Then you can use the same formula for standard error as in leave-one-out cross-validation.

Aki
 

Best,

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: K Fold Cross Validation - its explicit calculation
parts:
You can always divide by sample size.

It's a standard move in information theory from cross-entropy
to cross-entropy rate (just KL-divergence plus a constant divided
by sample size); Shannon used it in his original paper in
the 1940s to estimate bounds for the entropy rate of characters
in English, and it's still the standard measure for compression.
As far as I can tell, information theory is just probability theory
done on the log_2 scale.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: K Fold Cross Validation - its explicit calculation
parts:
If you have same number of posterior samples for each you can just concatenate them. If you have

nSamples x n1
nSamples x n2
nSamples x n3

then the combined matrix is

nSamples x (n1+n2+n3)

where n=n1+n2+n3 is the total number of observations

and then you proceed as if you would have been doing LOO (and in this case you don't need to divide by sample size as Bob suggests).

Aki

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: K Fold Cross Validation - its explicit calculation
parts:
I had the same question in doing my recent case study (which
has some related code). The average of logs isn't the
same as the log of the averages, so you want to do the average
on the linear scale. But you also want to avoid losing too
much arithmetic precision. So we calculate it as

log_sum_exp(lps) - log(N)

= log (exp(lps[1]) + ... + exp(lps[N]) / N)

So if the inputs are on the log scale, it does the linear
scale average (by exponentiating first), and then goes back
to the log scale.

It's just the sum(ps) / N on the log scale. So that if

lps = log(ps)

then

log_sum_exp(lps) - log(N) = log(sum(ps) / N)

- Bob

Hi Bob,

Thanks for your response; really helpful!

The only thing I am a little unclear about now, is how to use eqn. (23) in Vehtari et al. (2015) to estimate the standard error in prediction? 

As far as I understand it so far, we have got expression (20) by:

lpd_i = log_sum_exp(lps_i) - log(S) = log(sum(ps_i))/S

where S(=N) is the number of samples as given in the paper. To estimate elpd we just sum these across all folds, nFolds (or for LOO-CV, all data points):

elpd = sum_i=1^nFolds (lpd_i)

If all the above is correct, I want to know how we can go from the elpd above, to its standard error in eqn. (23)? Here there is another subscript "i", this time on the ELPD, not the LPD; I'm not sure exactly where this comes from? Expression (21) has no i subscript for example.

Best,

Ben

Sorry for the delay, I didn't notice earlier that discussion in this thread had continued. Equations 20 and 21 should have \hat{elpd}_i instead of \hat{lpd}_i.
lpd is defined by eq (2) as sum of lpd_i's and elpd is defined by eq (1) as sum of elpd_i's. \hat{elpd}_xval is approximation od elpd.

Thanks for being persistent and asking questions. I'll fix these in the manuscript and acknowledge your help.

Aki
